sources.title: A. A. Belavin, A. M. Polyakov, A. S. Schwartz, and Yu. S. Tyupkin, Pseudoparticle Solutions of the Yang–Mills Equations
sources.locator: The complete three-page paper, printed pp. 85–87. Equations (3)–(10) give the winding charge and action bound; equations (14)–(18) give a finite-action self-dual SU(2) charge-one field and an alternative gauge expression.

contents.name: Topological charge and boundary winding, equations (3)–(8)
contents.support: The source identifies the Euclidean charge integral with the degree of the asymptotic S3-to-SU(2) map. Its trace and sign conventions are translated to the library's anti-Hermitian B=-tr2 and c2 normalization in the local proof.

contents.name: Self-dual action lower bound, equations (9)–(13)
contents.support: The paper square-completes the Euclidean Yang–Mills action and identifies self-duality as the charge-one equality condition. The local proof independently derives the norm decomposition and the q=0 equality case.

contents.name: Regular finite-action charge-one SU(2) solution, equations (14)–(18)
contents.support: The paper constructs one explicit solution and discusses its asymptotic winding. It does not classify all charge-one solutions; the local example likewise makes no uniqueness claim.

sources.title: David Tong, TASI Lectures on Solitons: Instantons, Monopoles, Vortices and Kinks
sources.locator: Complete 39-page Lecture 1 PDF retrieved. §§1.1–1.1.2, printed pp. 6–10: action and trace convention, finite-action boundary behavior, winding charge, square completion, Bianchi equation, and the charge-one SU(2) connection with 't Hooft symbols.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §§1.1–1.1.1: topological charge, action bound, and Bianchi equation
contents.support: The note states the finite-action pure-gauge boundary condition and relates the charge to the winding on S3. It uses Hermitian generators; the authored mathematical definition records the library's anti-Hermitian trace sign separately.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §1.1.1, equations (1.6)–(1.8): square completion and field equation
contents.support: The source derives the bound, sign-dependent self-duality equality, and D_mu F^{mu nu}=0 from Bianchi. The local proof derives the corresponding differential-form equation for both duality signs.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §1.1.2, equations (1.9)–(1.11): a single SU(2) instanton
contents.support: The note gives the singular-gauge BPST formula and the self-dual/anti-self-dual 't Hooft symbols. The local example constructs a regular north-chart potential, verifies its south-chart transition, and computes the integral directly.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §1.1.1, equations (1.6)–(1.8): four-dimensional self-dual/anti-self-dual decomposition
contents.support: Tong uses the Hodge split in the action square-completion. The local item gives the full positively oriented orthonormal-coframe proof and extends it to a general finite-dimensional inner-product coefficient space.

sources.title: Stefan Haller, The Atiyah–Singer Index Theorem
sources.locator: Complete 141-page lecture-notes PDF retrieved. §II.4.1, printed pp. 88–89: Bianchi, closed trace curvature forms, transgression along a path of connections, and connection independence. Example II.4.5, printed pp. 91–92: determinant Chern form and c2 trace coefficient.

contents.name: §II.4.1, Proposition II.4.1(a)–(c): trace curvature classes
contents.support: The notes derive closedness from Bianchi and the induced endomorphism connection, then use the affine path between supplied connections and an explicit transgression form to prove independence. This corroborates the exact imported Chern–Weil interface; no connection-existence claim is borrowed.

contents.name: Example II.4.5: Chern determinant normalization
contents.support: The displayed determinant form det(I−R/(2πi)) gives c2=(tr(R∧R)−tr(R)∧tr(R))/(8π²); trace zero in the defining SU(2) representation leaves the stated coefficient.

sources.title: John W. Milnor and James D. Stasheff, Characteristic Classes (complete typeset book text)
sources.locator: Complete 333-page book text retrieved. Appendix C, printed pp. 308–309: curvature-polynomial representatives of Chern classes via line-bundle and splitting arguments. The sign-convention note on printed p. 306 was also inspected.

contents.name: Appendix C, Chern–Weil theorem and c2 comparison, printed pp. 308–309
contents.support: The book derives the Chern form class from the line-bundle normalization and the splitting argument. Its curvature convention differs by a sign from some classical conventions; degree two in curvature fixes the present c2 relation without importing the source's sign blindly.
